# Lean UX Canvas v2: frame the business problem and design experiments

Selected by Skill Harbor — short listing (the repo states no license, so no content is reproduced): @deanpeters's interactive skill for running Jeff Gothelf's Lean UX Canvas v2 — a one-page facilitation tool that frames work around a business problem to solve, not a solution to implement. The agent walks through the 8 boxes in order — Business Problem, Business Outcomes, Users, User Outcomes & Benefits, Solutions, Hypotheses (We-believe format), What's Most Important to Learn First, What's the Least Work to Learn Next — one question at a time with examples, quick-select options, and validation at each step, ending with a review and an export offer. It includes the key distinctions (Box 2 behavior-change metrics vs Box 4 empathy, solutions as hypotheses not commitments), common pitfalls (solution-first thinking, vague outcomes, confusing boxes 2 and 4, skipping experiments), and pointers to related skills. Honest caveats: interactive facilitation format — best run as a live workshop session (30–45 min); the companion `workshop-facilitation` protocol and the related component skills (problem-statement, proto-persona, jobs-to-be-done, epic-hypothesis, discovery-interview-prep) are referenced but not bundled; license not stated by the source repo — short listing with a link only, nothing copied. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
